Repo: C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Windows paths, PowerShell/Git-Bash environment). This is Kodely, an AI website builder. No new npm dependencies are allowed anywhere in this project.

FIRST: read docs/design-system.md in full — it is the binding contract for this whole product surface (tokens, components, and an audited "what does not exist" table). Also read app/globals.css in full to see the existing CSS custom-property token system (--surface*, --border-*, --brand*, --brand-chart-2, --brand-chart-3, etc. — many were added earlier this session) and the existing prefers-reduced-motion handling pattern (there's already a rule there — any new animation you add MUST respect it the same way). Also read components/ui/Card.tsx (SectionHeader is the current plain page-header component used across the portal) and app/(portal)/dashboard/new/PromptBox.tsx purely as a reference for this codebase's existing "glass" visual vocabulary (the `.glow-clip-a/-b` spinning-ring treatment in globals.css) — do NOT copy that spinning ring itself, it's specific to the AI-composer moment; your hero card needs its own calmer, distinct glass look (frosted/translucent panel, backdrop-blur, soft gradient sheen or border) that reads as "liquid glass," not as a copy of the composer.

THE ASK, in the customer's own words: "I want real hero cards for all of the pages, liquid glass. with icons/svg images or animated images in the cards correlating to the page they are on."

BUILD:
1. One new reusable component (place it in components/ui/, following that directory's existing naming conventions — e.g. PageHero.tsx) implementing a glassmorphism hero: a translucent, backdrop-blurred panel using ONLY the existing design-token system (never a hardcoded hex color that isn't already one of the established tokens), with a title, a description, and a slot for a per-page icon or small illustration. Where you add any animation (a subtle ambient glow, an icon micro-motion, etc.), gate it behind the same prefers-reduced-motion pattern already used elsewhere in app/globals.css.
2. Apply it to replace the current plain SectionHeader-based header on every real portal page under app/(portal)/dashboard/ (dashboard home, My Websites, Create, Templates, Usage — note Usage already has a Sparkles-accented header from earlier this session, integrate with that rather than duplicating effort — Billing, Domains, Support) and the three tabs under app/(portal)/settings/ (Account, Credits, Security). Do NOT touch anything under app/admin/ — that's explicitly out of scope.
3. Each page's hero must reuse that page's REAL existing title and description copy (do not invent new marketing copy) and use a lucide-react icon (already used everywhere in this codebase) or small inline SVG motif that genuinely correlates to that page's purpose — e.g. a home/house motif for the dashboard home, a stack/grid motif for "My Websites", a hammer or spark for "Create", a gallery/layout motif for "Templates", a chart/gauge for "Usage" (already has Sparkles — keep consistent), a receipt/card for "Billing", a globe/link for "Domains", a life-preserver or chat-bubble for "Support", a person/gear for the Settings tabs.
4. This is a PURELY visual/structural header change — every page's real data, real stats, real controls, and real functionality below the header must remain completely unchanged. Do not remove or alter any actual feature while doing this.
5. Both light and dark theme must look intentional — follow this codebase's established `:root` / `prefers-color-scheme` / `:root.dark` token pattern exactly (see app/globals.css for the pattern already used everywhere else this session) so the glass effect isn't just tuned for one theme.

STEPS:
1. Read every page you're going to touch first, and read docs/design-system.md before writing any component.
2. Build the one shared hero component.
3. Apply it consistently page by page — keep the visual language genuinely consistent (same glass recipe, same spacing rhythm), not eight ad hoc variations.
4. Run `cd /c/Users/edmem/kodely-prod && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` — both must be completely clean before you finish.

Report back: the exact list of every page you touched, and for each one, what icon/motif you chose and why it fits that page.

1	# Kodely product design system
2	
3	The contract for the customer-facing portal (`app/(portal)/**`) and the builder
4	(`app/projects/[id]/**`). Marketing pages (`app/page.tsx`, `/pricing`, `/blog`,
5	`/templates`, `/wizard`) are a **separate** system — do not repoint their tokens.
6	
7	## The one-sentence brief
8	
9	An AI website builder that happens to have a customer portal around it — not a
10	dashboard that happens to contain a builder. The primary action is always
11	"build something".
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Tokens
16	
17	Defined in `app/globals.css`, exposed to Tailwind via `@theme inline`. **Use the
18	Tailwind class, never a raw hex and never an arbitrary-value bracket.**
19	
20	### Surface
21	
22	| Class | Use |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `bg-canvas` | The page behind panels. Set by `AppShell`; pages never set it. |
25	| `bg-surface` | Cards, panels, the sidebar. |
26	| `bg-surface-2` | Hover, inset rows, quiet fills. |
27	| `bg-surface-3` | Track of a progress bar, the deepest step. |
28	| `bg-inset` | Code/preview wells. |

31

33	`border-line-strong` (emphasis, pending step outline)

63	`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
64	`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
65	`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
66	`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
67	`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
68	`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
69	`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Components (`components/ui/`)
74	
75	Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**
76	
77	| Component | Notes |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
80	| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
81	| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
82	| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`, and no page sets a title suffix (the group layout owns the
101	`"%s — Kodely"` template; a page declares only its own noun).
102	
103	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
104	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
105	
106	`SidebarFooter` carries the brand-gradient credits card, the theme toggle and
107	the bug/feature link (`/support?topic=bug`, `?topic=feature`). It appears in
108	both the desktop rail and the mobile drawer.
109	
110	**The credits card has no progress bar and no "X of Y" figure, deliberately.**
111	There is no allowance for the balance to be a fraction of — credits are bought
112	in packs and never expire — so a bar would have to invent a denominator. It
113	shows the balance and "about N more builds" from `averageBuildCredits()`.
114	**Anything else in the product showing credits must agree with it.** A card
115	elsewhere claiming a monthly total would contradict the rail sitting beside it.
116	
117	### Where the brand gradient may be used as a fill
118	
119	Three places, and nowhere else: the single `primary` button on a view, the
120	sidebar credits card, and the `/support` credits card. Not on headings, cards,
121	borders, icons or section dividers.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
126	
127	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
128	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
129	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
130	
131	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
132	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
133	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
134	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
135	and not a progress bar.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
140	
141	| Thing | Reality |
142	| --- | --- |
143	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
144	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |

149	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |

159	casually: `/legal/rights` and the data export both enumerate in writing
160	everything the database holds, so a new personal-data field silently makes two
161	published documents wrong.
162	
163	### The rule
164	
165	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
166	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
167	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.
